svg.title: Flow chart of the current depression hypothesis: stress drives the HPA axis (hypothalamus releases CRH, the pituitary gland releases ACTH, the adrenal gland releases cortisol), negative feedback is blocked because glucocorticoid receptors are desensitized, and the high stress hormones are toxic to neurons, inhibit BDNF and Reelin, break down neurons and synapses (especially GABA projections from the prefrontal cortex and hippocampus to the amygdala), and cause and perpetuate depression symptoms.
